key_insight: In an emergency medicine simulation benchmark, eight LLMs outperformed nine physicians across several assessed clinical skills and patient-facing communication measures.
clinical_relevance: Simulation-based evaluation may help assess medical AI beyond question-answer tests, but these findings do not establish safety or effectiveness in real emergency care.
method: An emergency medicine expert assessed clinical skills during simulated emergency visits.
An intern acting as a patient rated patient-facing performance.
A written examination tested general emergency medicine knowledge.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports significant AI advantages in history taking, investigation, diagnostic accuracy, treatment planning, comprehensibility, credibility, and empathy, but provides no numerical effect sizes.
watch_item: The small physician comparator group and simulated setting limit generalizability to real-world emergency care.
paper_title: Benchmarking Large Language AI Models Against Human Doctors Using an Emergency Medicine Simulation Approach
